A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MIRA study and provide readable text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–K. Revised, removed, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices J–K report original forecasting experiments, missing-data evaluations, and component/expert ablations. Figure 3 also reports training and expert-activation analyses.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendices J–K retain original forecasting, robustness, ablation, and expert-activation results, including revised benchmark values.

M1.justification: The CT-RoPE angle rule, expert routing, Neural ODE extrapolation, model configurations, and training losses remain unchanged. Appendix D recasts solver notation and stability documentation without establishing a different forecasting procedure or newly introduced component.

E1.justification: The five pretraining datasets, seven main out-of-distribution benchmarks, and WHO FluNet missingness scenario remain evaluated. Although FluNet disappears from the dataset list and Appendix G description, its Section 4.4 experiment and Table 4 remain.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in corresponding experiments, including the general-domain, medically pretrained, and full-shot models. Removing the supplementary Sundial description does not remove an evaluated baseline: both versions explicitly exclude Sundial.

E3.justification: The reported masking, interpolation, held-out evaluation, forecast horizons, model scales, and training budgets are retained. Both versions exclude other foundation models from the CinC 2012/2019 comparisons for the same interpolation reason. No revised evaluation protocol accompanies the changed scores.

E4.justification: V5 removes the pretraining-scalability analysis and Figure 3 training curves comparing model sizes. The missing-rate analysis, component ablations, expert-count accuracy/speed comparisons, and expert-activation heatmaps remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or formal significance tests. Averaging results across prediction lengths remains the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: Several primary benchmark outcomes change under unchanged reported settings. In Table 2, MIRA-large's CinC 2012 RMSE changes from 5.312 to 6.221, reversing its ordering against ContiFormer's unchanged 5.987; its MIT-BIH RMSE changes from 0.122 to 0.173. ContiFormer results on CinC 2019 and CDC-IHA and several MIT-BIH baseline and horizon-specific results also change. The reported 11% training-objective reduction is removed. These revisions materially alter the primary performance evidence.

T1.justification: Appendix C replaces the absolute lag in Equation 15 with a signed lag and replaces the matrix product in Equation 16 with a direct sum. Appendix D revises the adjoint equation, replaces an asymptotic error bound with an explicit inequality, and adds an explicit Lipschitz assumption to Theorem 1. These are localized mathematical revisions; the absolute-lag equivalence asserted after Equation 17 remains inconsistent.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction lower the claimed average forecasting-error reductions from 10%/7% to 8%/6% for out-of-distribution/in-distribution evaluation. The architectural, 454-billion-point corpus, and benchmark contributions retain their original scope.

C2.justification: V5 removes the interpretation of lower converged training loss as evidence of scaling benefits. Section 4.2 also changes its illustrative full-shot comparisons from CinC 2012/JH COVID-19 to MIT-BIH/CDC-IHA. The principal explanations concerning medical pretraining, robustness, expert specialization, and deployment/privacy limitations remain.

D1.justification: V5 adds a code repository link and states that the ODE dynamics are spectrally normalized, whereas v4 described normalization as something that could be applied. It removes Appendix G's dataset-statistics table, including counts, missing rates, and frequencies, together with the FluNet description and access footnote. Core hardware and training details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix H removes its short Sundial discussion, including its pretraining corpus and TimeFlow loss. Sundial remains cited and included in Table 6; the reference list, main related-work discussion, and central research positioning are otherwise unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites in the abstract, introduction, and Appendices B–D, including removal of the quantization summary bullets. Author affiliations and the conference footer are updated, and acknowledgments are added. The overall section and appendix organization remains stable.

P2.justification: Figure 3 loses its training-curve panel and presents the retained heatmaps beside wrapped text. The dataset-characteristics table is removed, existing tables are relocated and renumbered, and average-row shading is added to the detailed MIRA/full-shot results table.

improvement.justification: V5 adds a code pointer, partially repairs CT-RoPE mathematics, and aligns the reported MIT-BIH summary and appendix averages. However, it removes scaling evidence and dataset statistics while introducing inconsistencies: ContiFormer's CDC-IHA RMSE becomes 5.211 in Table 2 but remains 5.51 in Table 11, whereas v4 agreed. The revised MIT-BIH 64-step row also reports RMSE 0.070 below MAE 0.105. These mixed gains and reporting problems, without an explanation of the numerical revisions, prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
